NAHHAS:v4p235/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p235/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p235/r7.claim: The oath phrase means ships running, with يسرا describing an implied verbal noun: an easy running.
NAHHAS:v4p235/r7.anchor: عطف أي فالسفن الجاريات ( يسرا ) نعت لمصدر أي جريا يسرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r8.claim: The smooth-moving things are ships at sea.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب وغيره: هي السفن في البحر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r9.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r9.claim: Others say they are clouds moved by the wind.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r10.claim: Others call them the orbiting stars, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the wording accommodates all these readings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي الجواري من الكواكب، واللفظ يقتضي جميع هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r11.claim: يُسْرًا modifies an omitted verbal noun; adjectives of omitted verbal nouns function as circumstantial expressions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r11.anchor: ويسرا نعت لمصدر محذوف وصفات المصادر المحذوفة تعود أحوالا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r12.claim: يُسْرًا means with ease and little effort.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p171#2/r12.anchor: و: يسرا معناه: بسهولة وقلة تكلف،

JISHUMI:v9p6579/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6579/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6579/r7.claim: Jāriyāt is the plural of jāriyah and derives from the verb to run; dīn may mean recompense, religion, reckoning, or custom.
JISHUMI:v9p6579/r7.anchor: والجاريات: جمع جارية، وأصله من جرى يجري

JISHUMI:v9p6584/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r1.claim: The winds and clouds display God's great power and blessings, making them fit subjects for an oath.
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على عظيم قدرته تعالى في الرياح والسحاب وما فيها من النعم

ELMALILI:51:1-23/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:1-23/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:1-23/r6.claim: The things that sail smoothly may be ships and comparable means such as trains and automobiles.
ELMALILI:51:1-23/r6.anchor: gemiler ve emsâli trenler, otomobiller gibi

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r1.claim: The attributes in the opening oaths describe one subject, identified here as horses, and their ordered sequence follows a classical Arabic style; Ibn Zayyābah's couplet illustrates it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r1.anchor: all of them relate to horses, and deliberation would show that there is a sequence as well in their mention

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r3.claim: The phrase about gently moving things refers to winds, not ships; winds first blow fast with dust, then gather clouds and slow before bringing rain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p474/r3.anchor: The view of people who regard them to refer to ships is incorrect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p475/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p475/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p475/r1.claim: The varied effects of winds and clouds bring mercy to one people and storms as punishment to another.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p475/r1.anchor: For one nation, these merciful clouds descend as glad tidings; for another, these clouds stir up the torment of storms

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p481/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p481/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p481/r4.claim: Two oaths about wind effects and striped clouds substantiate two claims: the threatened punishment is certain, and the Hereafter's reward and punishment will occur.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p481/r4.anchor: Two things are sworn by at the beginning of the sūrah and after this two claims are stated

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r2.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas's report of a question by Ibn al-Kawwāʾ, ʿAlī identifies the winds, cloud-bearers, ships, and angels as the four oath referents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r2.anchor: فالمقسمات: الملائكة، هذا تفسير علي كرم الله وجهه على المنبر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r4.claim: Other views identify the coursing things as clouds driven by winds or as stars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r4.anchor: وقيل: الجاريات: السحاب بالرياح. وقيل: الجواري من الكواكب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r7.claim: يسرا means easy movement; the verbal noun works adjectivally with an omitted noun and is circumstantial on Sibawayh's analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p547/r7.anchor: ومعنى يسرا: جريا ذا يسر، أي سهولة. فيسرا مصدر وصف به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r2.claim: He allows all descriptions to refer to winds creating and carrying clouds and distributing rain; Abu Hayyan says different referents form successive groups, while one referent describes successive wind functions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد الرياح لا غير، لأنها تنشئ السحاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r3.claim: On the single-wind reading, the sequence is scattering dust, lifting clouds, moving them through the air, then distributing rain; a cited line likewise sequences raiding, taking booty, and return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p548/r3.anchor: أي ذرت أول هبوبها التراب والحصباء، فأقلت السحاب، فجرت في الجو

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r1.claim: After oaths by four groups of beings or events, verses 5–6 insist that the Day of Judgment is certain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r1.anchor: İlk dört âyette dört grup varlık veya olaya yemin edildikten sonra 5 ve 6. âyetlerde hesap gününün geleceğinden şüphe edilmemesi istenmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r2.claim: The plural participles used for the oath objects have prompted several different interpretations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r2.anchor: çoğul kalıbında sıfat fiiller kullanılarak üzerine yemin edilenler (zâriyât, hâmilât, câriyât, mukassimât) hakkında değişik açıklamalar yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r10.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r10.claim: The common interpretation of those that glide easily is ships; contemporary works also mention trains and cars, while other interpretations are wind-driven clouds or stars moving in their orbits.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r12.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r12.claim: Zamakhshari and Razi allow that the first four oath objects may be separate things or different qualities of one thing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r12.anchor: ilk dört âyette sayılanların ayrı şeyler ya da aynı şeyin farklı nitelikleri olabileceğini belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r13.speaker: Hz. Ali
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r13.claim: A saying transmitted from Ali supports the separate-entities interpretation: winds, clouds, ships, and angels distributing provision, respectively.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r13.anchor: Rüzgârlar, bulutlar, gemiler, rızıkları taksim eden melekler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r14.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r14.claim: Razi regards the interpretation of all four terms as different wind qualities as stronger: winds form clouds, carry water-vapor clouds heavier than mountains, drive those clouds, and distribute rain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r14.anchor: Râzî tarafından daha güçlü bulunan yoruma göre ise bu âyetlerde geçen kelimelerin anlamları şöyledir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r15.claim: The author surveys oath scholarship: besides Ibn Qayyim’s dedicated work, few older scholars wrote separately on Quranic oaths; contemporary Indian scholar Abd al-Hamid al-Farahi wrote a substantial introduction using that work and Razi.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r15.anchor: İbn Kayyim el-Cevziyye’nin et-Tibyân fî aksâmi’l-Kur’ân isimli eseri dışında eski âlimlerin bu konuda müstakil eserine rastlamadığını belirten muasır Hindistan âlimlerinden Abdülhamîd el-Ferâhî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r16.speaker: Abdülhamîd el-Ferâhî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r16.claim: Farahi’s Im’an fi Aqsam al-Qur’an studies general principles, analyzes Ibn Qayyim and Razi, discusses the history and human need for oaths with examples, and notes Arab oaths can honor the object or addressee, elevate the swearer, or draw on a belief that perjurers are cursed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r16.anchor: Araplar’ın yeminlerinde üzerine yemin edilene veya muhataba değer verme yahut bizzat yemin edenin mertebesinin yüceliğine dikkat çekme mânasının bulunduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r17.speaker: Abdülhamîd el-Ferâhî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r17.claim: Farahi says the essence and purpose of oaths is indication of meanings; glorification is not their primary Quranic purpose, though some oaths imply it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r17.anchor: Kasemin mahiyeti ve amacı “delâletler”dir, yani belirli mânaları göstermektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r18.speaker: Abdülhamîd el-Ferâhî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r18.claim: Farahi says the oath need not name an object sworn by; no unstated object must be supplied, and interpretation need not assume the object is being glorified.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r18.anchor: Yeminde “muksem bih”in (üzerine yemin edilenin) bulunması bile şart değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r19.speaker: Abdülhamîd el-Ferâhî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r19.claim: Farahi identifies the main purpose of an oath as reinforcing the speaker’s statement and showing firm resolve to do or refrain from something.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r19.anchor: Yeminde asıl amaç, yemin edenin sözü pekiştirmesi, bir şeyi yapıp yapmamayı kendisine gerekli kılıcı bir azim ve kararlılık izhar etmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r20.claim: The oaths draw the audience’s attention and invite reflection, emphasizing the seriousness of the subject.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r20.anchor: muhatapların dikkatini çekecek ve üzerinde düşünmelerini sağlayacak bir tarzda yemin edilerek konunun ciddiyetine vurgu yapıldığı açıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r21.speaker: Beyzâvî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r21.claim: The One capable of establishing extraordinary order and balance is also capable of fulfilling the promised resurrection of people after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r21.anchor: bu olağan üstü düzen ve dengeyi kurmaya kadir olan yüce Allah’ın vaad edilen ba‘s olayını yani insanların öldükten sonra diriltilmelerini gerçekleştirmeye de muktedir olduğuna işaret edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r22.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r22.claim: Swearing by important qualities without naming what bears them is an elegant concision that allows readers to imagine many possible referents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r22.anchor: mevsufları (nitelenenleri) açıklanmaksızın çok önemli ve üstün nitelikler üzerine yemin edildiğine göre bu âyetler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r23.claim: Because this surah repeatedly stresses earth and sky and says in verse 22 that provision and promises are in heaven, the first four oaths may point to life-critical laws, especially atmospheric events, biosphere changes, and angels assigned to enact them by divine will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:1/r23.anchor: ilk dört âyette de insan için hayatî önem taşıyan bazı yasalara, özellikle birtakım atmosfer olaylarına ve biyosferdeki değişkenlere

QASHANI:51:1-6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:51:1-6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:51:1-6/r3.claim: The gliding ones are souls moving easily through works and stations of nearness by these inspirations, or hearts flowing through seas of attributes.
QASHANI:51:1-6/r3.anchor: النفوس التي تجري في ميادين المعاملات ومنازل القربات بواسطة تلك النفحات والواردات يسرا

QASHANI:51:1-6/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:51:1-6/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:51:1-6/r6.claim: The oath by preparers, receptive capacities, and emanators establishes that their combined consequence must occur.
QASHANI:51:1-6/r6.anchor: أقسم بالمعدات والقوابل والمفيضات على أن مقتضى اجتماعها واجب الوقوع

QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r1.claim: The basmala is a word of might: remembering it empowers the tongue, knowing it makes the heart tremble in its company, and it conquers intellects and captivates lovers' spirits.
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r1.anchor: بسم الله كلمة عزيزة من ذكرها عز لسانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r2.claim: Outwardly, the winds carry burdens, the clouds carry rain, the ships run, and the angels distribute commands; the oath is by their Lord and His power over them, and its answer is that what is promised is true.
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r2.anchor: أي الرياح الحاملات { وقرا } أي السحاب

QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r7.claim: Just as sailors may carry poor passengers without charge in hope of the ship's safety, mystics hope to be carried on providence's ship through turbulent seas of power.
QUSHAYRI:v3p233/r7.anchor: فهؤلاء يرجون أن يحملوا في فلك العناية في بحار القدرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r3.claim: The smoothly running things are ships moving easily through water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r3.anchor: {فالجاريات يسرا} هي السفن تجري في الماء جريا سهلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r5.claim: God swears by these created things because they demonstrate His making and power.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p368#2/r5.anchor: أقسم بهذه الأشياء لما فيها من الدلالة على صنعه وقدرته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r5.claim: The ‘runners easily’ are clouds traveling freely across the sky, and also ships moving easily across the sea despite the weight of their cargo.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r5.anchor: وكذا جري السفن في باحة البحر بعد ثقلها بالوسق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r6.claim: The oath presents a causal sequence: wind disperses vapor, clouds carry it, and their travel culminates in water being divided among distant lands as mercy or punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p270/r6.anchor: وكان ذلك التفريق هو غاية الجري المترتب على الحمل المترتب على الذرو

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r3.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī says God swears by created wonders to strengthen belief and prompt reflection, whereas people swear by God as witness to a claim known to Him in secret and public.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r3.anchor: هذه أقسام يقسم الله بها ولا يقسم بها الخلق لأن قسم الخلق استشهاد على صحة قولهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r4.claim: Measured winds, suspended water-laden clouds, regulated ship movement, and angelic distribution all testify to a wise, powerful Creator; excess, cessation, or stillness can destroy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r4.anchor: ولو انقطعت بتسخير البحر لجريانها وتقدير الريح لها بما لو زاد لغرق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r7.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r7.claim: Ibn Barjān says every divine oath matches significant qualities in the object sworn by and guides whom God wills, though sensory appearances and distractions obscure its signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r7.anchor: ما أقسم بقسم إلا مطابقا معناه لمعان في المقسم من أجله بسراج منير يهدي به الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r8.speaker: البيضاوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r8.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī takes God’s power over extraordinary phenomena that defy ordinary nature as evidence of His power to resurrect.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271/r8.anchor: استدل باقتداره على هذه الأشياء العجيبة المخالفة لمقتضى الطبيعة على اقتداره على البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the oath and the assertion of judgment to Sūrat Qāf’s account of death and the afterlife, then cites warnings that God does not overlook wrongdoers and prolongs their respite to increase their sin.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r1.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه المواعيد الأخروية في سورة ق وعظيم تلك الأحوال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r4.claim: The majority identify the gently moving runners as ships sailing smoothly through water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r4.anchor: فالمشهور عن الجمهور -كما تقدم-: أنها السفن، تجري ميسرة في الماء جريا سهلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r5.claim: Some identify the runners as stars moving gently in their orbits, making the sequence rise from lower to higher created things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p414/r5.anchor: في أفلاكها، ليكون ذلك ترقيا من الأدنى إلى الأعلى

MUQATIL:51:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:51:1-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:51:1-6/r2.claim: The laden bearers are clouds heavy with water, while the smooth-moving ones are ships passing swiftly.
MUQATIL:51:1-6/r2.anchor: { فالحاملات وقرا } [آية: 2] يعني السحاب موقرة من الماء { فالجاريات يسرا } [آية: 3] يعني السفن مرت مرا

TABATABAI:51:5-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r1.claim: The four opening oaths exemplify world governance through causes on land, sea, and in the sky, completed by angels as intermediaries; together they swear by the general means through which cosmic affairs are administered.
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r1.anchor: فالآيات في معنى أن يقال أقسم بعامة الأسباب التي يتمم بها أمر التدبير في العالم

TABATABAI:51:5-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r2.speaker: علي عليه أفضل السلام
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r2.claim: Traditions from both Shiʿi and Sunni routes attribute the preceding interpretation of the four oaths to Ali.
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r2.anchor: وقد ورد من طرق الخاصة والعامة عن علي عليه أفضل السلام تفسير الآيات الأربع بما تقدم

TABATABAI:51:5-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r3.claim: Fakhr al-Razi says all four oaths most likely refer to winds; the author rejects this as remote and prefers the broader account of varied causes as more eloquent.
TABATABAI:51:5-7/r3.anchor: وعن الفخر الرازي في التفسير الكبير أن الأقرب حمل الآيات الأربع جميعا على الرياح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:1-8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:1-8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:1-8/r1.claim: The winds scatter dust, clouds carry water, and ships sail easily.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:1-8/r1.anchor: الرياح التي تذرو التراب. { فالحاملات وقرا } وهي السحاب تحمل الماء. { فالجاريات يسرا } السفن تجري في البحر بيسر

SAMIN-DURR:51:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:51:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:51:3/r1.claim: يسرا may be a verbal noun for easy running, a circumstantial phrase meaning easy or eased, or “ease itself” as emphasis.
SAMIN-DURR:51:3/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مصدرا من معنى ما قبله أي: جريا يسرا، وأن تكون حالا أي: ذات يسر أو ميسرة أو جعلت نفس اليسر مبالغة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r3.speaker: علي
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r3.claim: Ali identifies the smoothly sailing objects as ships.
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r3.anchor: قال: (فالجاريات يسرا) قال الفلك. قال: (فالمقسمات أمرا) قال الملائكة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r5.claim: The listed objects are genitive under an oath, whose answer is that what people are promised is true.
ZAJJAJ:v5p51/r5.anchor: (والذاريات) مجرور على القسم، المعنى أحلف بالذاريات وبهذه الأشياء، والجواب: (إنما توعدون لصادق (5)

NASHR:v2p215/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p215/r6.speaker: النهرواني عن عيسى بن وردان
NASHR:v2p215/r6.claim: In فالجاريات يسرا, al-Nahrawani's transmission from Isa ibn Wardān through Abu Amr makes the sin quiescent.
NASHR:v2p215/r6.anchor: واختلف عن عيسى بن وردان عنه في فالجاريات يسرا في الذاريات فأسكن السين فيها النهرواني عنه

QIRAAT-ER:51:3:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:51:3:3#1/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:51:3:3#1/r1.claim: The skn reading places ḍamma on sīn instead of sukūn, yielding fuller yusuran; it may reflect an archaic nominal pattern or dialectal variant.
QIRAAT-ER:51:3:3#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: ḍamma on sīn instead of sukūn — yusuran vs yusran; a fuller vocalization

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r1.speaker: أبو الطفيل
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r1.claim: Abū al-Ṭufayl says Ali invited questions, claiming he could answer anything about the future and knew whether every verse came by night or day, on plain or mountain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r1.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال شهدت عليا وهو يخطب وهو يقول سلوني فوالله لا تسألوني عن شيء يكون إلى يوم القيامة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r2.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r2.claim: Ali interprets the four oaths as winds scattering dust, clouds, ships sailing easily, and angels distributing commands.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r2.anchor: فقال علي ويلك سل تفقها ولا تسل تعنتا الذاريات ذرو الرياح ﴿ فالحاملات وقرا ﴾ قال السحاب

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r3.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r3.claim: Ali rebukes Ibn al-Kawwāʾ, telling him to ask in order to learn rather than to provoke.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r3.anchor: فقال علي ويلك سل تفقها ولا تسل تعنتا الذاريات ذرو الرياح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r5.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r5.claim: Ali says Dhū al-Qarnayn was neither prophet nor king, but a righteous servant who loved and sincerely served God, called his people to guidance, and was struck on each side of his head in turn.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r5.anchor: أفرأيت ذا القرنين أنبيا كان أم ملكا قال ولا واحد منهما ولكنه كان عبدا صالحا أحب الله فأحبه وناصح الله فناصحه دعا قومه إلى الهدى فضربوه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r6.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r6.claim: Ali identifies the rainbow as a sign between Noah and his Lord and as protection from drowning.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r6.anchor: قال أفرأيت هذا القوس ما هي قال علامة كانت بين نوح بين ربه وأمان من الغرق

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r7.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r7.claim: Ali describes al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr as a structure in the seventh heaven beneath the Throne, entered daily by seventy thousand angels who do not return.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p241/r7.anchor: قال أفرأيت البيت المعمور ما هو قال ذلك الصرح في سبع سماوات تحت العرش يدخله كل يوم سبعون ألف ملك لا يعودون

ALUSI-FULL:v27p2#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p2#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p2#4/r1.claim: The smooth-running vessels are ships sailing easily toward their destination.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p2#4/r1.anchor: أي جريا سهلا إلى حيث سيرت وهي السفن

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r6.claim: The things running easily may be ships, winds in their courses, or stars in their stations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r6.anchor: فالسفن الجارية في البحر سهلا، أو الرياح الجارية في مهابها

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r7.claim: يسرا describes an omitted verbal noun: an easy running.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r7.anchor: صفة مصدر محذوف أي جريا ذا يسر

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r9.claim: If the oath terms are different beings, ف orders them by increasing evidence of power; if one kind, it orders the actions by which winds form, carry, move, and distribute clouds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:1-5/r9.anchor: فإن حملت على ذوات مختلفة بالفاء لترتيب الأقسام

DURR-FULL:v7p613/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p613/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v7p613/r7.claim: Ali identifies the smoothly sailing as ships.
DURR-FULL:v7p613/r7.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه في قوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p172/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p172/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p172/r2.claim: The things running easily are ships.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p28#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p28#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p28#2/r1.claim: The smoothly sailing things are ships moving easily through the water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p28#2/r1.anchor: يعني السفن تجري ميسرة في الماء جريا سهلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.claim: Ali identifies the smoothly sailing ones as ships and those distributing commands as angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r2.anchor: {فالجاريات يسرا} ؟ قال: السفن. [قال] (4) : {فالمقسمات أمرا} ؟ قال: الملائكة (5) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r3.claim: In al-Bazzar's report through Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, Umar says the Prophet identified the winds, ships and angels by these oaths while answering Ṣubaygh al-Tamimi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r3.anchor: قال: جاء صبيغ التميمي إلى عمر بن الخطاب فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، أخبرني عن {الذاريات ذروا} ؟ فقال: هي الرياح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r4.claim: Umar had Ṣubaygh beaten one hundred times, confined him, then beat him another hundred and barred people from his company; he later permitted him back after he swore his troubling thoughts were gone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r4.anchor: ثم أمر به فضرب مائة، وجعل في بيت، فلما برأ (6) [دعا به و] (7) ضربه مائة أخرى،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report raised to the Prophet weak; its nearest sound form is a report stopping at Umar. He says Umar punished Ṣubaygh because the questioning appeared stubborn and contentious, and notes al-Bazzar's criticism of two transmitters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p413#2/r5.anchor: قلت: فهذا الحديث ضعيف رفعه، وأقرب ما فيه أنه موقوف على عمر،

BURSEVI:v9p119/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p119/r6.claim: Yusran qualifies an omitted verbal noun: the ships sail easily and smoothly through the sea.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r6.anchor: يسرا صفة لمصدر محذوف أي فلسفن الجارية في البحر جريا يسيرا

BURSEVI:v9p119/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
BURSEVI:v9p119/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the sea's provision is in an angel's hand; if the angel neglected it, the sea would cover the earth.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال : البحر رزق بيد ملك

BURSEVI:v9p119/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v9p119/r8.claim: A Prophetic hadith permits riding the sea only for a campaign, pilgrimage, or minor pilgrimage, saying fire lies beneath the sea, followed by sea and fire beneath it. No grading is given.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث لا يركبن رجل البحر إلا غازيا أو حاجا أو معتمر فإن تحت البحر نارا

BURSEVI:v9p119/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r9.speaker: كعب
BURSEVI:v9p119/r9.claim: Kaʿb says that nightly the seas ask God for leave to drown sinners, but He commands them to remain still.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r9.anchor: وقال كعب : ما من ليلة إلا والبحار تشرف على الخلائق

BURSEVI:v9p119/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r10.speaker: سليمان بن داود
BURSEVI:v9p119/r10.claim: When Solomon ibn David asked about the sea's ruler, a sea creature emerged from sunrise to noon and said half of it had not yet come out; Solomon sought refuge from the sea and its ruler.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r10.anchor: وسأل سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام عن ملك البحر فخرجت إليه دابة من البحر

BURSEVI:v9p119/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p119/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p119/r11.claim: The ships signify lovers and beloved ones whose sails catch the winds of providence, carrying them easily through the sea of divine unity.
BURSEVI:v9p119/r11.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن سفن وجود المحبين المحبوبين شراعها مرفوعة إلى مهب رياح العناية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r6.claim: Yusran means running with ease, that is, easy running.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r6.anchor: ومعنى ( يسرا ) : جريا ذا يسر ، أي ذا سهولة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r9.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r9.claim: In a pulpit exchange with Ibn al-Kawwa, Ali identified the oath figures respectively as winds, clouds, ships, and angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r9.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال وهو على المنبر : سلوني قبل أن لا تسألوني ، ولن تسألوا بعدي مثلي ، فقام ابن الكواء فقال : ما الذريات ذروا ؟ قال : الرياح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r13.claim: Another possible reading takes all four oath descriptions as winds: they form and carry clouds, move them through the air, and distribute rain by directing them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : الرياح لا غير ؛ لأنها تنشىء السحاب وتقله وتصرفه ، وتجري في الجو جريا سهلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r14.claim: On the first interpretation, the fāʾs order the winds, the clouds they drive, ships moved by their blowing, and angels apportioning provisions through rain and sea trade.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r14.anchor: فبالسحاب الذي تسوقه ، فبالفلك التي تجريها بهبوبها ، فبالملائكة التي تقسم الأرزاق بإذن الله من الأمطار وتجارات البحر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r15.claim: On the wind-only reading, the sequence follows the winds' actions: they blow, scatter dust and gravel, move clouds, spread them in the air, and apportion rain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p398/r15.anchor: لأنها تنشىء السحاب وتقله وتصرفه ، وتجري في الجو جريا سهلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r11.claim: One view says these are ships sailing easily by wind where directed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r11.anchor: السفن تجري بالريح يسرا إلى حيث سيرت

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r12.claim: Another view says these are clouds, moved where God directs or moved easily.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p360/r12.anchor: أنه السحاب , وفي جريها يسرا على هذا القول وجهان

MUJAHID:v2p615/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p615/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p615/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the vessels that sail smoothly as ships.
MUJAHID:v2p615/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ والذاريات ذروا ﴾ قال الرياح ﴿ فالحاملات وقرا ﴾ قال السحاب يحمل المطر ﴿ فالجاريات يسرا ﴾ قال السفن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p176#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p176#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p176#3/r1.claim: The running things are ships; yusrā means running with ease.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p176#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ فالجاريات ﴾ الفلك ﴿ يسرا ﴾ جريا ذا يسرى اى ذا سهولة

QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r5.claim: The flowing things are ships driven easily by winds to wherever they are directed.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r5.anchor: السفن تجري بالرياح يسرا إلى حيث سيرت

QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r6.claim: An alternative identifies the flowing things as clouds, which God directs across regions and lands.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r6.anchor: وقيل: السحاب وفي جريها يسرا على هذا القول وجهان: أحدهما إلى حيث يسيرها الله

QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r7.claim: On the cloud interpretation, yusran can mean ease of movement, a familiar usage among Arabs.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r7.anchor: الثاني هو سهولة تسييرها وذلك معروف عند العرب، كما قال الأعشى:

QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r8.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r8.claim: Al-Aʿsha compares a woman's easy-paced walk to a cloud's movement, neither slow nor rushed.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:3/r8.anchor:
كما قال الأعشى:
كأن مشيتها من بيت جارتها
مشي السحابة لا ريث ولا عجل

STUDYQURAN:51:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r1.speaker: Bḍ, JJ, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies those coursing easily as ships moving across the ocean’s surface.
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r1.anchor: Ships that course upon the surface of the ocean (Bḍ, JJ, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:51:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r2.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies them as planets moving through their stations.
STUDYQURAN:51:3/r2.anchor: or the planets that run through their stations (Bḍ)

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r1.claim: The prophetic call invited polytheists to God’s sole lordship through warning and good news, especially warning of worldly destruction and everlasting punishment in the Hereafter.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r1.anchor: كانت الدعوة النبوية تدعو الوثنية إلى توحيد الربوبية وأن الله تعالى هو ربهم ورب كل شيء

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r2.claim: Accountability and recompense in the Resurrection are central to the mission; without them, belief in divine oneness and prophethood would have no effect.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r2.anchor: إذ لولا الحساب والجزاء يوم القيامة كان الإيمان بالوحدانية والنبوة لغى لا أثر له

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r3.claim: The polytheists persistently deny resurrection because they see its denial as undoing monotheism and prophethood, making their rejection a route to invalidate the religion and messenger.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r3.anchor: وكانوا يتعنتون بإنكار المعاد والإصرار على نفيه والاستهزاء به من أي طريق ممكن لما يرون أن في بطلانه بطلان الأصلين الآخرين

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r4.claim: The sūra opens and closes on resurrection as the Day of Recompense promised truthfully by God; proofs of lordship establish that promise and answer the deniers.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r4.anchor: ولذلك لما انساق الكلام إلى الاحتجاج عليه احتجت بأدلة التوحيد من آيات الأرض والسماء والأنفس

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r5.claim: The sūra is Meccan, as its context shows, and no one has disputed this.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r5.anchor: والسورة مكية لشهادة سياق آياتها عليه ولم يختلف في ذلك أحد

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r7.claim: The opening section affirms the promised recompense, calls its denial conjecture, and describes the Day and the conditions of the pious and deniers.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r7.anchor: الفصل الذي أوردناه من الآيات مفتتح الكلام يذكر فيه أن الجزاء الذي وعدوه صدق وإنكارهم له وتعنتهم بذلك تخرص

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r12.claim: The oath is by ships sailing easily over the seas.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r12.anchor: عطف عليه وإقسام بالسفن الجارية في البحار بيسر وسهولة

TABATABAI:51:1-4/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r14.claim: The successive oaths intensify the affirmation that people will be recompensed for their deeds.
TABATABAI:51:1-4/r14.anchor: وفي الآيات إقسام بعد إقسام يفيد التأكيد بعد التأكيد للمقسم عليه وهو الجزاء على الأعمال

TABRISI:51:1-4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r8.speaker: علي
TABRISI:51:1-4/r8.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa while preaching, Ali identified the scatterers as winds, burden-bearers as clouds, smooth runners as ships, and distributors as angels; Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also transmit this interpretation.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r8.anchor: سأل أمير المؤمنين عليا ع وهو يخطب على المنبر فقال

TABRISI:51:1-4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:1-4/r12.claim: The smooth runners are ships gliding easily over water wherever they are directed.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r12.anchor: السفن تجري ميسرة على الماء جريا سهلا إلى حيث سيرت

TABRISI:51:1-4/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:51:1-4/r13.claim: Alternative referents are clouds moving where God sends them or the seven planets: Sun, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r13.anchor: وقيل: هي السحاب تجري يسرا إلى حيث سيرها الله

TABRISI:51:1-4/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:1-4/r15.claim: God swears by these things for their great benefits to people and the signs they contain of His oneness and artistry.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r15.anchor: أقسم الله تعالى بهذه الأشياء لكثرة ما فيها من المنافع للعباد

TABRISI:51:1-4/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:51:1-4/r16.claim: One view construes the oath as being by the Lord of these things, since an oath may only be made by God.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن التقدير فيها القسم برب هذه الأشياء لأنه

TABRISI:51:1-4/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:1-4/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:51:1-4/r17.claim: Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah say people may swear only by God, while God may swear by whichever creatures He wills.
TABRISI:51:1-4/r17.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله ع إنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يقسم إلا بالله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p425#7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p425#7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p425#7/r1.claim: The smoothly moving things are ships, gliding easily through the water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p425#7/r1.anchor: يعني السفن تجري ميسرة في الماء جريا سهلا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r1.claim: The running ones are ships moving easily through the water.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r1.anchor: أي السفن تجري في الماء جريا سهلا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p420#4/r2.claim: An alternative gloss says they run maysara, meaning they are made subservient.

MAJAZ:v2p225/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p225/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p225/r4.claim: The smoothly sailing ones are ships.

ITQAN:v4p529#5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p529#5/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ITQAN:v4p529#5/r1.claim: Umar reports that the oath's جاريَاتِ يُسْرًا are ships, والذاريات are winds, and المقسمات are angels; he says he would not say so without hearing the Prophet.
ITQAN:v4p529#5/r1.anchor: أخرج البزار عن عمر بن الخطاب قال ﴿ والذاريات ذروا ﴾ هي الرياح ﴿ فالجاريات يسرا ﴾ هي السفن ﴿ فالمقسمات أمرا ﴾ هي الملائكة

BURHAN:v2p114/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.claim: They classify the opening oath sequences of al-ʿAdiyat and al-Dhariyat as basit meter.
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.anchor: ﴿ والعاديات ضبحا فالموريات قدحا ﴾ ونحوه قوله
